subject: [AMBER] Amber installation error for Intel Xeon machine (ubuntu 20.04)

messages.author: Chen, Guoquan
messages.body:
Hi,
I downloaded Amber20 and Amber20 Tools, and have successfully installed it with GCC only and GCC+Cuda.
Now when I tried to install it for Intel Xeon machine (Icelake Xeon, with Ubuntu 9.3.0-17ubuntu1~20.04). Here is the error message I got from
build/run_cmake                                          (#the only change is from GNU to INTEL for compiler)
-- **************************************************************************
-- Starting configuration of Amber version 20.0.0...
-- CMake Version: 3.16.3
-- For how to use this build system, please read this wiki:
--
http://ambermd.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/CMake
-- For a list of important CMake variables, check here:
--
http://ambermd.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/CMake-Common-Options
-- **************************************************************************
-- Amber source found, building AmberTools and Amber
CMake Error: Generator: execution of make failed. Make command was: /usr/bin/gmake cmTC_6554c/fast &&
CMake Error at cmake/CompilationOptions.cmake:62 (message):
Could not detect target architecture from compiler.  Does the compiler
work?
Call Stack (most recent call first):
cmake/AmberBuildSystem2ndInit.cmake:38 (include)
CMakeLists.txt:111 (include)
It appears that something is wrong when checking the target architecture in CMake.  How to proceed?
Thanks for any help,
gqchen
From: Chen, Guoquan
Sent: Monday, November 1, 2021 5:26 PM
To: amber-subscribe.ambermd.org<mailto:amber-subscribe.ambermd.org>
Subject:

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Tue, Nov 02, 2021, Chen, Guoquan wrote:
>
>  I downloaded Amber20 and Amber20 Tools, and have successfully installed
>  it with GCC only and GCC+Cuda.
>Now when I tried to install it for Intel Xeon machine (Icelake Xeon, with
>Ubuntu 9.3.0-17ubuntu1~20.04). Here is the error message I got from
>build/run_cmake (#the only change is from GNU to INTEL for compiler)
>CMake Error at cmake/CompilationOptions.cmake:62 (message):
>  Could not detect target architecture from compiler.  Does the compiler
>  work?
Well: does your compiler work?  Are icc and ifort in your PATH?  Can you
compile a simple program with them?
You might report how you installed the compilers (using oneAPI?).
What happens if you use the Icelake machine, but set the compiler back to
GNU?  It's certainly possible that TargetArch.cmake doesn't handle your CPU,
but I'd be surprised...
....dac
